name: Alcohol-free mouthwash

lead: Alcohol-free mouthwash is any oral rinse made without ethanol. People choose it for regular breath and gum care when alcohol rinses feel drying or irritating, or when they prefer to avoid alcohol.

The antibacterial action comes from other ingredients such as CPC, essential oils or plant extracts. Trials exist for individual formulations with CPC, propolis, chitosan-curcuminoid and essential oils. Many newer products omit alcohol partly over a possible oral cancer link, which Wikipedia describes as inconclusive.

paras: People swap it in for a conventional rinse as a daily after-brushing step, often picking by active ingredient and by how comfortable it is for a dry mouth.
Hospital outbreaks of Burkholderia cepacia infection have been traced to contaminated alcohol-free mouthwash. Performance varies by product, since the category is defined only by what it leaves out.

angle.text: People choose alcohol-free rinses for regular breath and gum care, often for dry-mouth comfort or to avoid ethanol. How well each works depends on its active ingredient, such as CPC or essential oils.

lead: Alcohol-free mouthwash is a category of oral rinse formulated without ethanol, often with cetylpyridinium chloride, essential oils, herbal extracts or other active ingredients. Wikipedia notes many newer products omit alcohol partly over concern about a possible link to oral cancer, which it describes as inconclusive, and to suit people who avoid alcohol.[1]

Its looksmaxxing relevance is mainly breath and dry-mouth comfort. Trials of alcohol-free rinses include CPC, propolis, chitosan-curcuminoid and essential oil formulations.[2][3][4][5] Hospital outbreaks of Burkholderia cepacia infection traced to contaminated alcohol-free mouthwash have also been published.[6][7][8]

paras: A phase II study of 25 adults tested an alcohol-free 5 percent propolis rinse for plaque and gingivitis.[2] A randomised double-blind crossover study compared two alcohol-free CPC rinses.[3] A randomised trial compared an alcohol-free chitosan-curcuminoid rinse with chlorhexidine in denture stomatitis.[4] A 2011 trial examined an essential oil rinse with and without alcohol in a 3-day plaque model. Laboratory work has tested chitosan against decay-related bacteria.[9]

In 2005, investigators described a multistate outbreak of Burkholderia cenocepacia colonisation and infection in hospital patients tied to an intrinsically contaminated alcohol-free mouthwash, and earlier and later hospital outbreaks were reported.[6][7][8][5] Wikipedia notes that alcohol-containing mouthwash can worsen dry mouth.[1]

Randomised trials of specific alcohol-free formulations exist for plaque, gingivitis and denture stomatitis.[2][3][4] Direct comparisons of alcohol-containing and alcohol-free versions of the same rinse are limited in the sources reviewed, apart from a short plaque model.

timeline.event: Outbreak of Burkholderia cenocepacia infection linked to contaminated alcohol-free mouthwash investigated across several US states.[6]
